| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἕλεν ἄνδρα (4.457, αἱρέω of killing) | "took a man" (`l` "Antilochus took a man of the Trojans": Τρώων goes with ἄνδρα, and "Antilochus of the Trojans" would make him a Trojan) | "killed a Trojan" (+ note: ‘take’ = kill) | "slew" in `l` (hides the idiom), "captured", "caught" |
| κορυστής (ἄνδρα κορυστήν, 4.457; κόρυς "helmet", cf. κορύσσω "arm") | "helmeted warrior" | "helmeted warrior" (+ note: ‘armed’ is the other reading) | "armed man", "man in armour", "helm-wearer"; κορύσσω keeps "arm" (ἱπποκορυσταί, κεκορυθμένος) |
| πρόμαχος (ἐνὶ προμάχοισι 4.458; διὰ προμάχων 4.495; πρόμαχοι 4.505) | "front-fighters" | "foremost fighters" | "champions", "vanguard", "men in the front line", "foremost" alone |
| τὸν δὲ σκότος ὄσσε κάλυψε(ν) (4.461 = 4.503 = 4.526, whole-line death formula; τόν and ὄσσε both accusative, whole and part) | "and darkness covered his two eyes" | "and darkness covered his eyes" | "black night", "mist", "shrouded", "veiled"; "darkness" is σκότος, "night" is kept for νύξ; ὄσσε is the dual "two eyes" in `l`; the same English at all three places (the ν of κάλυψεν at 461 is not a difference) |
| ἤριπε (4.462, 4.493) | "crashed down" | "crashed down" | "fell" (kept for πίπτω, πεσών), "toppled", "collapsed"; ἐρείπω "crash down" |
| ἐνὶ κρατερῇ ὑσμίνῃ (4.462) | "in strong battle" | "in strong battle" | Odyssey table’s κρατερὴ ὑσμίνη "strong battle", unchanged |
| βελέων (ὑπ’ ἐκ βελέων 4.465; βέλος 4.498; βελέων ἐρωήν 4.542) | "shafts" · "shaft" | "shafts" · "shaft" | "missiles" (the Odyssey’s alternative), "arrows" (ὀϊστοί), "darts"; follows the Iliad’s βέλος "shaft" (1.382, 4.185) |
| κρείων Ἐλεφήνωρ (4.463) | "lord Elephenor" | "Lord Elephenor" | follows the table’s κρείων Ἀγαμέμνων "lord Agamemnon"; "ruling", "king" |
| 4.464, Χαλκωδοντιάδης μεγαθύμων ἀρχὸς Ἀβάντων (= 2.541) | "Chalcodon’s son, commander of the great-hearted Abantes," | "the son of Chalcodon, commander of the great-hearted Abantes" | the packet’s English from iliad-012, unchanged |
| μίνυνθα (4.466) · ὁρμή | "briefly" · "drive" | "only a little while" · "his drive" | "short-lived" (kept for μινυνθάδιος), "impulse", "onset", "rush" (kept for ἐρωή); μίνυνθα is the adverb "for a short time" |
| ξυστῷ χαλκήρεϊ (4.469) | "polished, bronze-fitted spear" | "polished, bronze-fitted spear" | "lance", "javelin" (ἄκων), "smooth shaft"; ξυστόν "scraped, smoothed" (ξύω), a spear; χαλκήρης keeps "bronze-fitted" (the Odyssey’s χαλκήρεα δοῦρα, iliad-019 κυνέῃ χαλκήρεϊ) |
| οὐτάω (οὔτησε 4.469; οὖτα 4.525) | "wounded" | "stabbed" | "struck" (kept for τύπτω, τύψε at 4.531), "pierced" (πέρησε), "speared"; οὐτάω is a thrust from close at hand, so `l` keeps the root sense "wounded" and `i` says how |
| βάλλω of a weapon (4.459, 4.473, 4.480, 4.499, 4.501, 4.519, 4.527) | "hit" | "hit" | "struck", "threw", "hurled"; follows the table’s οὐδ’ ἔβαλόν μιν "and I did not hit him" (3.368) |
| λῦσε γυῖα (4.469) | "loosed his limbs" | "loosed his limbs" | "unstrung his knees", "slackened his limbs", "made him fall"; the idiom for killing is kept whole and the note says what it means |
| ἀργαλέον ἔργον … Τρώων καὶ Ἀχαιῶν (4.470–471) | "a work was wrought grievous, of Trojans and Achaeans" | "a grievous work of Trojans and Achaeans was wrought" | "struggle", "fighting" (loses ἔργον "work", the table’s word at 2.436), "labour" |
| ἐδνοπάλιζεν (4.472; δνοπαλίζω, "toss about", sense not certain) | "tossed about" | "tossing about" (+ note: sense not certain) | "shook", "hustled", "wrestled", "hurled" (each picks one guess) |
| ἠΐθεον θαλερόν (4.474) | "a young man, flourishing" | "a flourishing young man" | "blooming" (reserved for θαλερὸς γάμος), "abundant" (θαλερὸν δάκρυ), "lusty", "in the bloom of youth"; ἠΐθεος "unmarried young man"; θαλερός of persons is "flourishing", from the root of θάλλω "thrive" |
| θρέπτρα (4.478) | "the repayment for rearing" | "repay … for his rearing" | "recompense for their care", "the price of their nursing", "nurture-gifts"; τρέφω "rear" |
| αἴγειρος · εἱαμενή · ἕλος (4.482–483) | "poplar" · "water-meadow" · "marsh" | "poplar" · "water-meadow" · "marsh" | "aspen", "willow", "black poplar" (adds a species); "meadow" alone, "low ground", "flat"; "swamp", "fen" |
| ἁρματοπηγός · ἴτυς (4.485–486) | "chariot-builder" · "wheel-rim" | "chariot-builder" · "wheel-rim" | "wagon-maker", "wright", "chariot-maker"; "felloe", "tyre", "hoop"; ἁρματοπηγός from ἅρμα + πήγνυμι |
| ἀζομένη (4.487) | "drying out" | "lies drying out" | "withering", "seasoning", "growing old", "honoured" (each decides a disputed sense); ἄζομαι "dry up" |
| ἐξενάριξεν (4.488) | "despoiled" | "killed and stripped of his armour" | "slew", "plundered", "stripped" alone; ἐξεναρίζω is kill and strip, from ἐνάρα "spoils" |
| διογενής (Αἴας διογενής, 4.489) | "Zeus-sprung" | "Zeus-born" | Odyssey and Iliad table’s διογενής, unchanged (listed because here it is of Ajax) |
| αἰολοθώρηξ (4.489, of Antiphus) | "of the glancing breastplate" | "with the glancing breastplate" (+ note: gleaming or flickering not known) | "bright-corsleted", "shimmering-mailed", "with the gleaming breastplate" (each decides the sense); αἰόλος keeps "glancing" (παναίολος "all-glancing"), θώρηξ "breastplate" |
| ἀκοντίζω (4.490, 4.496, 4.498) | "cast" (with ὀξέϊ δουρί, "cast with a sharp spear") | "cast his sharp spear" | "hurled", "threw" (kept for βάλλω in its throwing sense), "let fly" (kept for ἀφείη), "javelined"; ἀκοντίζω from ἄκων "javelin" |
| ἅλιον βέλος (4.498; ἅλιος "in vain", not ἅλιος "of the sea") | "a shaft in vain" | "did not send his shaft in vain" | "idle", "wasted", "futile"; the note says it is a different word from ἅλιος "of the sea" |
| κόρση · κρόταφος (4.502) | "the side of the head" · "temple" | "the side of the head" · "temple" | "temple" for κόρση (κρόταφος keeps "temple"), "brow", "skull" |
| φαίδιμος Ἕκτωρ (4.505) | "glorious Hector" | "glorious Hector" | "shining", "splendid" (reserved for ἀγλαός); follows the Odyssey table’s φαίδιμος "glorious" |
| κέκλετ’ ἀΰσας (Τρώεσσι δὲ κέκλετ’ ἀΰσας, 4.508) | "gave orders to the Trojans, shouting" | "shouted orders to the Trojans" | "called to", "cried out to"; follows the table’s κέκλετο "gave orders to" |
| ὄρνυσθ’ ἱππόδαμοι Τρῶες (4.509, whole-speech opening) | "Rouse yourselves, horse-taming Trojans" | "Rouse yourselves, Trojans, tamers of horses" | "Up, Trojans", "Rise", "Stir yourselves"; follows ἱππόδαμος "horse-taming" / "tamer of horses" (Odyssey, iliad-017) |
| μηδ’ εἴκετε χάρμης (4.509) | "do not yield from the joy of battle" | "do not give way … in the joy of battle" | "do not give up the fight" (loses χάρμη); the table’s χάρμη "the joy of battle" (4.222) |
| λίθος χρὼς … ταμεσίχροα (4.510–511) | "stone the skin" · "skin-cutting" | "their skin is not stone" · "skin-cutting" | "flesh" (kept for σάρξ), "hide", "body"; "flesh-cutting", "slicing"; χρώς "skin", ταμεσίχροα from τάμνω + χρώς |
| χόλον θυμαλγέα πέσσει (4.513) | "heart-paining anger he cooks" | "broods over an anger that pains his heart" | "digests", "nurses", "chews over" (each decides the figure); the Greek metaphor is cooking, kept in `l`; θυμαλγής keeps the Odyssey’s "heart-paining" |
| Διὸς θυγάτηρ κυδίστη Τριτογένεια (4.515) | "the daughter of Zeus, most glorious Tritogeneia" | "the daughter of Zeus, most glorious Tritogeneia" | "Triton-born", "third-born"; the Odyssey’s own phrase (3.378, odyssey-012), unchanged |
| δεινὸς θεός (4.514) | "the dread god" | "the dread god" | "terrible", "awesome", "formidable"; follows the Odyssey table’s δεινός "dread" |
| μοῖρα πέδησε (4.517) | "portion bound" | "fate bound" | "doom", "destiny"; follows the table’s μοῖρα "portion" in `l` and "fate" in `i` (21.24), with πεδάω "bind, fetter" |
| χερμάδιον ὀκριόεν (4.518) | "a jagged rock" | "a jagged rock" | "boulder", "stone" (kept for λᾶας and λίθος), "flint"; ὀκριόεις "jagged" |
| ἀγὸς ἀνδρῶν (Θρῃκῶν ἀγὸς ἀνδρῶν, 4.519) | "leader of Thracian men" | "leader of the Thracian men" | "chief", "captain"; ἀγός "leader" as for ἡγεμών, ἡγήτωρ |
| λᾶας ἀναιδής (4.521) | "the shameless stone" | "the ruthless stone" | the Odyssey table’s λᾶας ἀναιδής (11.598), unchanged |
| ἄχρις ἀπηλοίησεν (4.522; ἀπαλοιάω, rare) | "utterly crushed" | "crushed … utterly" | "smashed", "ground to pieces", "broke through"; ἄχρις "utterly" |
| χολάδες (4.526) | "bowels" | "bowels" | "entrails" (kept for σπλάγχνα), "guts", "intestines" |
| ἀπεσσύμενον (4.527) | "rushed away" | "rushed away" | "fleeing", "darting off", "running"; ἀποσεύομαι "dart off" |
| στέρνον (4.528, 4.530) · στῆθος (4.480) | "breast" · "chest" | "breast" · "chest" | the pair already in use (iliad-022: στέρνοιο "breast", στῆθος "chest"); listed so that they stay apart |
| ἀγχίμολον δέ οἱ ἦλθε (4.529) | "close by him came" | "came close by him" | "close up", "near", "at once", "right behind"; the half-line is Odyssey 15.95 (odyssey-072), whose English is kept |
| ἐσπάσατο (4.530) | "pulled out" | "pulled … out" | "drew" (kept for ἐρύσσατο, ἕλκω), "tore", "dragged"; σπάω |
| ἀκρόκομοι (Θρήϊκες ἀκρόκομοι, 4.533; ἄκρος + κόμη, exact fashion not known) | "topknotted" | "topknotted" (+ note: exact fashion not known) | "long-haired" (κάρη κομόωντες), "with hair on top", "crested" (λόφος); each picks one guess |
| δολίχ’ ἔγχεα (4.533) | "long spears" | "long spears" | "far-reaching", "long-shadowed" (δολιχόσκιον); δολιχός "long", ἔγχος "spear" |
| πελεμίχθη (4.535) | "was shaken" | "gave ground, reeling" | "was driven back", "trembled", "was made to quake"; πελεμίζω "shake" |
| τετάσθην · τέταντο (4.536, 4.544) | "had been stretched out" | "lay stretched out" | "were laid low", "lay", "had fallen"; pluperfect passive of τείνω "stretch", kept in `l` and rendered as the state in `i` |
| ἀνὴρ ὀνόσαιτο μετελθών (4.539) | "a man make light of the work, going among it" | "a man going among that work would … make light of it" | "find fault with" (LSJ’s other gloss, which the Odyssey table turns down for ὄνομαι), "belittle", "despise"; follows the Odyssey table’s ὄνομαι "make light of" (17.378, 5.379); ἔργον keeps "work" |
| ἄβλητος καὶ ἀνούτατος (4.540) | "unhit and unwounded" | "unhit and unwounded" | "unscathed", "unharmed", "untouched"; βάλλω "hit", οὐτάω "wound" |
| δινεύοι κατὰ μέσσον (4.541) | "might wheel about in the middle" | "might wheel about in the midst" | "whirl", "move round", "stroll"; δινεύω "whirl, wheel about" |
| ἐρωή (βελέων … ἐρωήν, 4.542) | "rush" | "force" | "onrush", "flight", "fury"; as in iliad-016 (ἀνδρὸς ἐρωήν "the man’s rush" / "the man’s force") |
